newsitem.title: INDIA: India state tightens security ahead of strike.
newsitem.headline: India state tightens security ahead of strike.

text.p: India's eastern state of West Bengal tightened its security on Thursday ahead of a one-day strike called by the opposition Congress party against alleged corruption by the local communist government.

Banks, schools, shops and offices are likely to remain closed on Friday during the strike called against alleged siphoning off state funds by the government led by the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M).
"If CBI can inquire into the fodder scam in Bihar then why not initiate an enquiry on the funds in West Bengal," said Somen Mitra, president of the state unit of the Congress party in West Bengal.
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is currently investigating Laloo Prasad Yadav, chief minister of the neighbouring eastern state of Bihar, and 55 others in a $280 million corruption case.
The case has come to be known as the "fodder" scandal because of alleged diversion of animal welfare funds. Yadav denies any wrongdoing in the case.
West Bengal is home to the world's oldest democratically elected communist government which completed its 20 years in power last month.
